editorial:
Imagine being a teenager who feels completely ignored by your dad, who is more obsessed with his job at a nuclear plant than with his own son. That is exactly where you find yourself in this story. You follow a frustrated kid who finally snaps and decides to wreck some gear at the plant just to get some attention. It is a gritty, emotional ride that captures that feeling of being lost and angry at the world. The movie feels like a road trip through a young man's soul, blending family drama with a search for meaning in a world that feels cold and mechanical.

You will probably love how the acting feels real and not forced. The pacing starts off tense and then slows down as the main character finds his spiritual path, which gives you some breathing room. While some parts might feel a bit slow for people who want constant action, the emotional payoff is worth it. If you enjoy stories about growing up and finding yourself, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick to rent on Apple TV for a quiet night in, or you can grab the 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: After spending a long time on the road and meeting different people, the teen finally lets go of his anger. He stops running from his problems and finds a sense of inner peace. In the final scenes, he reconciles with his father, showing that he has matured. He chooses a path of forgiveness instead of hate, ending the movie on a hopeful note where the family finally starts to heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about rebellious teens finding their way in life.
